QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the standard enthalpy change of following reaction: $$\mathrm{C_2H_4(g) + 3O_2(g) \rightarrow 2CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(l)}$$ If $\Delta_f H^\circ (\mathrm{C_2H_4}) = -52$ kJ mol⁻¹, $\Delta_f H^\circ (\mathrm{CO_2}) = -390$ kJ mol⁻¹, $\Delta_f H^\circ (\mathrm{H_2O}) = -286$ kJ mol⁻¹.

Solution.S:
$\Delta_r H^\circ = \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{reactants})$.

Products: $2\mathrm{CO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$.

Reactants: $\mathrm{C_2H_4} + 3\mathrm{O_2}$ (oxygen is in standard state, so $\Delta_f H^\circ = 0$).

$$\Delta_r H^\circ = [2(-390) + 2(-286)] - [(-52) + 3(0)]$$

$$= (-780 - 572) - (-52) = -1352 + 52 = -1300 \text{ kJ}$$

Thus the correct option is B: -1300 kJ.
